title: Proportional backpressure and tenant-prioritized degradation for downstreams
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Customer-facing SLOs are vulnerable when downstreams (Redis, Kafka, SQL DBs) experience partial failures or congestion. Current circuit breaker and blunt shedding strategies either recover capacity too slowly or cause disproportionate impact to tenants. We need a tiered, proportional approach that reduces pressure smoothly, prioritizes critical traffic/tenants, and supports safe multi-region failover without a hard, immediate cutoff.

Proposal summary:
1) Proportional backpressure controller: compute a continuous backpressure factor per downstream and per region derived from short-window SLO risk score (error budget burn rate, queue lengths, latency percentiles). The factor is 0..1 and scales admission/concurrency, connection pool sizes, and batch sizes incrementally instead of binary open/closed.
2) Tenant-prioritized request scoring: each request receives a compact score (priority, SLA tier, estimated token cost, operation type read/write). Admission decisions use the score to shape request acceptance—low-scoring requests are delayed, routed to degraded paths, or dropped depending on severity.
3) Connection pool elasticity + soft drains: implement pool trimming where idle and lower-priority connections are closed first; active high-priority leases are preserved. When tightening pool limits, new leases are subject to proportional admission until load stabilizes.
4) Degraded read/write modes: reads can fall back to cached/approximate responses (e.g., prefix KV from local LRU; stale-but-fast), while writes may be buffered to an LSM-style local durable queue with prioritized eviction and best-effort asynchronous replay to primary DB/Kafka.
5) Cross-region hedging and directional failover: use region-specific risk factors to decide whether to hedge (duplicate to another region) or to redirect traffic. Avoid symmetric failover loops by adding lease-based region preference.
6) Observability + automation: expose the backpressure factor and per-tenant acceptance rates to console dashboards and alert when the burn-rate thresholds are hit. Automatic rollback and gradual relaxation policies when error budget recovers.

Why this is different:
- Smooth degradation avoids cliff-effects observed in recent incidents where whole tenants lost service when a single circuit tripped.
- Prioritized buffering maintains meaningful guarantees for paying customers and critical control-plane traffic.
- Local durable queueing for writes prevents sync-blocks when DB replicas lag or are temporarily isolated.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: Redis (primary read cache), Kafka producers/consumers, and SQL write paths used by inference metadata and billing. Pool trimming logic also touches the runtime's connection lifecycle manager.
- Non-goal: redesigning the full tenancy billing model or changing SLA tiers. We will read existing billing metadata to compute priority but not modify tiers in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Backpressure factor computed and emitted for Redis/Kafka/DB in prod-metrics (per region)
Admission controller enforces proportional acceptance at 3 backpressure levels (soft/medium/hard) with measurable reduction in downstream QPS without full circuit trips
Connection pool supports priority-aware trimming and emits pool-size change events
Local write queue persists at least 1GB across restarts and replays with ordering guarantees per-tenant
End-to-end integration test that simulates a DB node slow-down and shows critical tenant success rate >= 95% while best-effort tenants degrade
Runbook updated with remediation steps and failback procedures
implementation_notes: Metric inputs: 60s error budget burn, 1m p95 latency, current queue depth, consumer lag (Kafka), replica sync gap (DB)
Backpressure factor formula: clipped sigmoid of normalized burn-rate * (1 + latency_penalty) — tune in staging
Admission point: API gateway + runtime admission layer + per-tenant token bucket fallback
Pool trimming strategy: close idle connections starting from lowest-priority tenant; maintain min-reserve for control-plane and admin tenants
Local write queue format: append-only segments with per-tenant index for replay ordering; use same encryption-at-rest keys as other runtime artifacts
Failure modes: if local queue exceeds configured cap, apply tenant-priority eviction and emit events to billing/alerts
rollout_plan: Week 1: implement instrumentation and expose backpressure factor metric in staging
Week 2: implement admission controller + pool trimming in canary cluster (single region)
Week 3: enable tenant-prioritized buffering for writes; run chaos tests (delay DB responses, drop redis)
Week 4: gradual traffic ramp to 10% then 50% of production traffic with telemetry validation; enable multi-region hedging flags behind FF
Post-rollout: monitor 2 weeks, iterate thresholds, and document SLO changes
metrics: Local write-queue length and replay success rate
Incident indicators: number of circuit events, error-budget burn-rate
tests: Unit: backpressure math module with synthetic burn rates
Integration: admission controller + pool trimming with synthetic Redis latency injected
Chaos: simulate a DB replica isolation and ensure prioritized traffic remains >= 95%
Load: run 2x traffic and validate proportional shedding reduces downstream QPS to target levels
